To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a de novo germlin mutation in the SKIL gene may be associated with the development of an intraductial papillary mucinous pancreatic neoplasm in the context of congenital hyperinsulemia.

a 3 day old patient with congenital hyperinulinism and an IPMN with high grade dysplasia was found to have an SKIL gene mutation that was present in the tumor but not in the surrounding pancreatic parenchyma or in the patient's blood.

a neonate presented with congenital hyper-insulinism and an intraductalan papillary mucinous tumour (IPMN) of the pancreas, and whole exome sequencing revealed a de novo mutation in SKIL, which is a known driver mutation of pancreatic cancer.

the role of SKIL in the development of IPMN and congenital hyperinsulism.

the IPMN in our patient was likely caused by a de novo mutation in the KRAS gene.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a neonate with a pancreatic tumor and congenital hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycemic had a de novo SKIL germline mutation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a pancreatic tumor in an infant with severe congenital hyperinsulism should lead to consideration of the possibility that the pancreatic tumor may have arisen from the hyperplastic lesion that is responsible for the hyperinsulinism.
pancreatic cystic tumors in neonates with severe hypoglycaemia should be considered for surgical resection.
